lab.about: A runaway sock flees the washing machine through the laundry room: rubber ducks, soap bars, cats, bubbles and a hairdryer. It speeds up every second.
lab.controls: Phone: tap the right side to jump (again for a double jump), hold the left side to duck. PC: SPACE / up to jump, down to duck.
lab.name: Sock Escape
lab.tagline: A sock flees the washing machine. Jump, duck, survive the Dryer of Doom.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: You are a light pulse in a waveguide. Collect photons and grow, but don't hit the walls, your own tail or scattering defects. Every 5 photons adds defects and speed.
lab.controls: Phone: swipe to steer. PC: arrows or WASD.
lab.name: Waveguide Snake
lab.tagline: You're a light pulse. Eat photons, grow, dodge scattering defects.

versions.notes: Godot remake of the Laugh Lab built-in game, with swipe controls.

lab.about: You're late for your cleanroom slot. Every 14 seconds is a new room with new hazards: pits, flying deadlines, hopping HF, falling reviews. Grab wafers for bonus metres.
lab.controls: Phone: tap to jump, tap again in the air to double jump. PC: SPACE or up.
lab.name: Cleanroom Parkour
lab.tagline: Late for your cleanroom slot. Jump pits, deadlines and falling reviews.

versions.notes: Godot remake of the Laugh Lab built-in game, five rooms.

lab.about: You are a photon trapped in a VCSEL, and the only way out is to hop across Bragg mirrors while Reviewer 2 sweeps the room with a laser pointer. Survive 72 seconds and 6 levels.
lab.controls: Phone: drag on the left half to move, JUMP button to jump. PC: arrows to move, SPACE or up to jump.
lab.name: Escape the Cavity
lab.tagline: You're a photon stuck in a laser. Hop the mirrors, grab carriers, survive 6 levels.

versions.notes: Godot remake of the Laugh Lab game: difficulty setting, 6 levels with the Lab Cat.

web: v2 (2026-10-19): difficulty setting, 6 levels with a new Lab Cat, broader jokes

lab.about: Photons refuse to turn, so you summon a pocket black hole to bend them into the fiber. Don't let them fall in, and watch out for the goose, the monolith and the nebula.
lab.controls: Phone: touch and hold where the black hole should be. PC: hold the mouse, or move with arrows and hold SPACE.
lab.name: Bend It Like Einstein
lab.tagline: Hold to summon a pocket black hole and bend photons into the fiber.

versions.notes: Godot remake of the Laugh Lab game: difficulty setting, nebula fog level.

web: v2 (2026-10-19): difficulty setting, real fog level, broader jokes

lab.about: Deliver party invitations across the galaxy by slingshotting between moving planets. Let go of your orbit at the right moment. You have to planet ahead.
lab.controls: Tap anywhere or press SPACE to let go of the orbit.
lab.effort: Web effort 7 of 8: Studio (built and playtested)
lab.name: Orbit Courier
lab.tagline: Slingshot between moving planets to deliver party invitations.

versions.notes: Godot remake of the Laugh Lab game, with a difficulty setting.

lab.about: Steer a Viking longship through fjords, gusts, icebergs and a kraken, without once asking for the way. Grab loot, keep your three shields.
lab.controls: Phone: hold the screen above or below the ship to steer. PC: up / down.
lab.effort: Web effort 7 of 8: Studio (built and playtested)
lab.name: Never Ask for Directions
lab.tagline: Steer a Viking longship past fjords, icebergs and a kraken. Don't ask.

versions.notes: Godot remake of the Laugh Lab game. Sails sideways to fit a landscape screen.

lab.about: Swing a very expensive laser beam across a night sea so captains can see the rocks, without lighting up the smugglers or feeding the sea serpent. Each night adds fog, storms, smugglers or the serpent.
lab.controls: Phone: touch where the beam should point. PC: move the mouse, or left / right.
lab.effort: Web effort 7 of 8: Studio (built and playtested)
lab.name: Lighthouse Keeper
lab.tagline: Swing a very expensive laser so ships see the rocks. Mind the serpent.

versions.notes: Godot remake of the Laugh Lab game: fog, storm, smugglers and the serpent.

lab.about: Bounce from a Twente rooftop to the Moon, dodging honking geese, space junk and meteoroids, with stroopwafels as syrup-powered rocket fuel. Stomp geese from above.
lab.controls: Phone: hold the left or right side of the screen to steer. PC: left / right. Jumping is automatic.
lab.effort: Web effort 7 of 8: Studio (built and playtested)
lab.name: Escape Velocity
lab.tagline: Bounce from an Enschede rooftop to the Moon. Stomp geese, eat stroopwafels.

versions.notes: Godot remake of the Laugh Lab game: 5 zones, windmills, geese and the Moon.

lab.about: Eleven years of sword school, then someone invented the crossbow, so you chase the inventor through five eras of history: a castle, Viking seas, a Roman aqueduct, a Dutch polder and his tower. Progress saves at every level and at the boss.
lab.controls: Phone: drag on the left half to move, JUMP and SWORD buttons. PC: arrows, SPACE / up to jump, X or J to swing. Swing at bolts and axes to parry them.
lab.length: 20-30 min: 5 levels and a boss, with saves
lab.effort: Web effort 8 of 8: Masterpiece (several playtest rounds)
lab.name: The Last Knight
lab.tagline: Chase the crossbow inventor through five eras. Parry, stomp, honk.

versions.notes: Godot remake of the Laugh Lab game: 5 eras, the boss, save and continue at every level and at the boss.

web: v2 (2026-10-19): save and continue at every level and at the boss

lab.about: The classic sliding-number puzzle: every swipe slides all tiles, equal tiles merge into their sum and a new tile appears. Make a 2048 tile, then keep going for a high score. Easy has a 5x5 board and unlimited undo, Normal 4x4 with 3 undos, Hard 4x4 with no undo and more 4s.
lab.controls: Swipe anywhere on the board. Undo and New game buttons on the right. PC: arrow keys or WASD, U to undo.
lab.tagline: Swipe to slide numbered tiles; equal tiles merge. Reach 2048.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: A fresh Sudoku every time, generated on your phone and always with exactly one solution. Easy gives 44 numbers, Normal 34, Hard 27. Pencil notes, hints, undo, and clashing numbers turn red.
lab.controls: Tap a cell, then a number on the pad. Notes writes pencil marks, Erase clears, Hint fills a cell. PC: arrows, 1-9, N for notes, H for hint, U to undo.
lab.name: Sudoku
lab.tagline: Fill the 9x9 grid: every row, column and box holds 1 to 9 once.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: Open every cell that hides no mine. Each number counts the mines around it. Easy is 10x7 with 10 mines, Normal 14x9 with 22, Hard 16x10 with 35. The first tap is always safe.
lab.controls: Tap to open, long-press or Flag mode to flag a mine. Tap a number whose mines are flagged to open the rest around it. PC: click, right-click to flag.
lab.name: Minesweeper
lab.tagline: Open every safe cell; the numbers tell you where the mines are.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: Classic Klondike solitaire. Move cards between the seven piles in alternating colours, counting down, and build each suit from Ace to King on the foundations. Easy deals one card at a time with unlimited undo, Normal one card, Hard three cards at a time.
lab.controls: Drag cards, or tap a card to send it where it fits best. Tap the deck to draw. Undo and Auto finish buttons on the right.
lab.name: Solitaire
lab.tagline: Klondike patience: build the four suits up from Ace to King.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: Picross: the numbers next to each row and column tell how many filled cells there are, in order. Fill the right cells to reveal a picture. Easy 5x5, Normal 8x8, Hard 10x10.
lab.controls: Tap a cell to fill it, long-press or Cross mode to mark it empty. Drag to fill a line. Hint and Undo buttons on the right.
lab.name: Nonogram
lab.tagline: Fill the grid from the number clues to reveal a hidden picture.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: Every tap flips a light and the four next to it. Turn the whole board dark in as few moves as you can. Puzzles always have a solution. Easy 4x4, Normal 5x5, Hard 6x6.
lab.controls: Tap a light. Undo, Hint and Restart buttons on the right.
lab.name: Lights Out
lab.tagline: Tap a light to flip it and its neighbours. Turn them all off.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: The 15 puzzle: slide tiles into the empty space until they are in order. Easy 3x3, Normal 4x4, Hard 5x5. Every shuffle can be solved.
lab.controls: Tap a tile next to the gap (or in its row or column) to slide it. PC: arrow keys.
lab.name: Sliding Puzzle
lab.tagline: Slide the tiles back into order, 1 to 15.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: Remove matching pairs of tiles. A tile is free when nothing lies on top of it and its left or right side is open. Easy has fewer tiles and layers. Every deal is built so it can be solved.
lab.controls: Tap two matching free tiles. Hint, Shuffle and Undo buttons on the right.
lab.name: Mahjong Solitaire
lab.tagline: Match pairs of free tiles until the stack is gone.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: The warehouse puzzle: walk around and push crates onto the marked spots. Crates can only be pushed, one at a time. Every level is built backwards from the solved warehouse, so it can always be solved, and each solved level unlocks a bigger one. Easy has 2 crates, Normal 3, Hard 4.
lab.controls: Swipe to take one step (and push), or tap a square to walk there. Undo, Restart and Skip level buttons on the right. PC: arrow keys, U to undo, R to restart.
lab.length: 1-10 min per level, endless levels (saves progress)
lab.name: Sokoban
lab.tagline: Push every crate onto a target. You can push, never pull.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: Draw a pipe from each dot to its partner of the same colour. Pipes can't cross, and in the end every square should be filled. Easy 5x5, Normal 7x7, Hard 9x9; every puzzle is generated with a solution.
lab.controls: Drag from a dot to draw its pipe. Drag back over a pipe to shorten it. Hint and Restart buttons on the right.
lab.name: Flow
lab.tagline: Connect dots of the same colour with pipes that never cross.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: A falling-block game: turn and slide the pieces so they fill whole rows, which then disappear. It gets faster every 10 lines. Clear 20 rows to win on Easy, 40 on Normal, 60 on Hard, then keep going for a high score.
lab.controls: Swipe left or right to slide, tap to rotate, swipe down to drop. Or use the on-screen buttons. PC: arrows, up or X to rotate, space to drop.
lab.length: 3-15 min per game (saves after every piece)
lab.name: Block Stacker
lab.tagline: Falling blocks: rotate, slide and clear full lines.

versions.notes: First version.

lab.about: Drop your discs into the 7 columns and line up four in a row, across, down or diagonally, before the computer does. Easy plays loosely, Normal thinks a few moves ahead, Hard looks deep.
lab.controls: Tap a column to drop a disc. Undo and New game buttons on the right.
lab.name: Connect Four
lab.tagline: Drop discs and get four in a row before the computer does.

versions.notes: First version.

external.name: Outpost Assault
external.tagline: Tower defense: build gatling, cannon and missile turrets to hold the outpost.
external.about: Waves of infantry, tanks and helicopters march on your outpost. Tap the empty turret slots to build gatling, single-shot or missile turrets, and repair or replace them between waves. Survive three growing waves to win. Made by Quiver (quiver.dev) as an open-source Godot 4 template.
external.controls: Tap a turret slot to build, tap a turret to repair, replace or remove it (its range shows while selected). Drag with one finger to move the map; pinch or use the + / - buttons to zoom; II pauses. PC: click, middle-drag, scroll wheel, ESC.
external.credit: Outpost Assault by Quiver (quiver.dev), github.com/quiver-dev/tower-defense-godot4. Code: MIT license. Art: CC BY 4.0. Font: Akashi by Ed Merritt. Added to Lab Arcade with touch controls and a back button.

versions.notes: Quiver's Outpost Assault (commit 1cbd622, 2026-08-21), security-reviewed, with touch pan / pinch zoom and a way back to the arcade.

external.name: 3D Platformer
external.tagline: Run, double-jump and collect coins across floating 3D platforms.
external.about: A small, polished 3D platformer by Kenney: run across floating islands, double-jump between platforms, break bricks from below, ride falling platforms and collect every coin. Fall off and you start again.
external.controls: Drag on the left half to walk, JUMP (tap again in the air for a double jump), < and > turn the camera, + and - zoom. PC: WASD, space, arrow keys.
external.credit: Starter Kit 3D Platformer by Kenney (kenney.nl), github.com/KenneyNL/Starter-Kit-3D-Platformer. Code and art: MIT license. Added to Lab Arcade with touch controls and a back button.

versions.notes: Kenney's Starter Kit 3D Platformer (commit 3fa8a04, 2026-03-12), security-reviewed, with an on-screen stick and buttons.

external.name: Kenney Racing
external.tagline: Kart racing with boosts, bananas and shells on five tracks.
external.about: Kenney's toy truck goes kart racing: five tracks, three computer drivers, 3 laps, boost pads, item boxes (mushroom, banana, shell), a drift boost and a start boost. Race one track, drive the whole cup, or race your own ghost in time trial. Version 1.0 is the original free drive.
external.controls: Drag on the left half and point where the truck should go; it steers and drives that way. ITEM uses your item, REVERSE backs up, II pauses. PC: WASD or arrow keys.
external.length: About 2 minutes a race, 10 for the cup
external.credit: Starter Kit Racing by Kenney (kenney.nl), github.com/KenneyNL/Starter-Kit-Racing. Code and art: MIT license. Added to Lab Arcade with touch controls and a back button.

versions.notes: Kenney's Starter Kit Racing (commit 2f2e5f2, 2026-08-21), security-reviewed, with on-screen steering and gas / brake buttons.

Kart racing: 5 tracks, 3 computer drivers (Easy / Normal / Hard), laps, positions, finish line and score, boost pads, item boxes with mushroom, banana and shell, drift and start boosts, a 5-track cup, and time trial against the ghost of your best time per track. GAS / BRAKE replaced by REVERSE and ITEM; help page inside the game.

external.name: Tactical RPG
external.tagline: Turn-based battle on a 3D board: move your units, attack, outlast.
external.about: A small turn-based tactics battle in the style of Final Fantasy Tactics: your team and the enemy team take turns on a 3D grid. Pick a unit, move it across the tiles, attack an enemy in range, then wait. The enemy plays back. Win by defeating every enemy unit.
external.controls: Tap a unit to pick it, then Move or Attack and tap a tile. Wait ends that unit's turn, End turn ends yours. Arrow buttons move the camera, << >> turn it, + and - zoom. PC: mouse, WASD, Q / E, wheel.
external.effort: Open-source demo by ramaureirac and mbusson
external.credit: Godot Tactical RPG by @ramaureirac and @mbusson, github.com/ramaureirac/godot-tactical-rpg. MIT license. Added to Lab Arcade with tap controls, camera buttons, a win / lose ending and a back button.

versions.notes: Godot Tactical RPG (commit cfe785e, 2026-02-21), security-reviewed, with tap controls, camera buttons and a victory / defeat ending.

external.name: Open RPG
external.tagline: A little pixel-art RPG: explore a town, solve a puzzle, fight in turn-based battles.
external.about: A short JRPG-style adventure by GDQuest: a small robot wakes up in a town, helps a ghost in the woods, talks to the townsfolk, collects tokens for an adoring fan, opens chests and doors, solves a wand puzzle and fights turn-based battles with a party of animals.
external.controls: Tap where to walk, tap people and objects to talk or use them, tap to continue a conversation. In battle tap an action, then tap the enemy (or friend) to use it on. BACK undoes a choice. PC: arrow keys / WASD, space, mouse, Esc.
external.effort: Open-source demo by GDQuest and contributors
external.credit: Godot Open RPG by GDQuest and contributors, github.com/gdquest-demos/godot-open-rpg. Code MIT, art and music by the authors listed in CREDITS.md. Uses Dialogic 2 (MIT). Added to Lab Arcade with tap-to-pick targets, a BACK button and a back-to-arcade button.

versions.notes: Godot Open RPG (commit d59f2f7, 2026-10-13) with Dialogic 2, security-reviewed, with tap controls for battles and a back button.

external.name: City Builder
external.tagline: Lay roads, parks and houses square by square and build a little 3D town.
external.about: A calm city-building sandbox by Kenney: pick roads, pavements, parks and buildings, turn them the way you like and place them on the grid. Every piece costs money, there's no rush and no game over; your town saves itself so you can keep building later.
external.controls: Tap a square to build the piece shown top right. < and > pick the piece, TURN rotates it, DEL switches to removing (tap a square to clear it), NEW starts over. Drag to move around, pinch to zoom, twist two fingers to turn the view. PC: click, WASD, Q / E, R, Delete, mouse wheel.
external.credit: Starter Kit City Builder by Kenney (kenney.nl), github.com/KenneyNL/Starter-Kit-City-Builder. Code and art: MIT license. Added to Lab Arcade with touch controls, autosave and a back button.

versions.notes: Kenney's Starter Kit City Builder (commit 4535092, 2026-03-12), security-reviewed, with touch building, pan / pinch / twist camera and autosave.

external.name: Deck Crawler
external.tagline: A Slay-the-Spire-style roguelike: build a deck and fight up a map of battles.
external.about: Pick the Warrior or the Assassin and climb a branching map of battles, shops, campfires and treasure rooms. Each turn you draw a hand of cards and spend mana to attack, block and apply statuses; enemies show what they're about to do. Win battles to add cards and relics to your deck and beat the boss at the top. The run saves as you go.
external.controls: Drag a card up onto the battlefield to play it; attacks that need a target show an arrow, drop it on an enemy. Drag a card back down to cancel. Tap END TURN when you're done. Drag the map up and down, tap a lit room to go there. II pauses. PC: the mouse, Esc pauses.
external.effort: Open-source game made as a Godot tutorial series
external.credit: Roguelike Deckbuilder by Adam Gulacsi (guladam), github.com/guladam/deck_builder_tutorial. Code and art: MIT license. Added to Lab Arcade with touch controls, a safe save loader and a back button.

versions.notes: guladam's Roguelike Deckbuilder (commit 91b408b, 2024-10-16), security-reviewed, with touch map scrolling, a pause button, a back button and a safe save loader.

external.name: Open RTS
external.tagline: Real-time strategy: mine, build a base, train tanks and drones, defeat the AI.
external.about: A small real-time strategy game in 3D. Your workers mine crystals and build structures; command centers, vehicle factories and aircraft factories train workers, tanks and drones. Fog of war hides the map until your units see it, and a computer opponent builds up at the same time. Destroy everything it owns to win. Maps for 2 to 4 players.
external.controls: Tap one of your units to select it (tap it again quickly for all of its kind). Then tap the ground to move, or an enemy or crystal to attack or mine. Drag to move the view, pinch to zoom. BOX then drag: select a group. ALL / NONE select the army or nothing. Build and train with the buttons at the bottom; when placing a building, tap where it goes (drag to turn it), STOP to cancel it. II: menu. PC: the original mouse and keyboard controls.
external.credit: Open RTS by Lampe Games, github.com/lampe-games/godot-open-rts. Code: MIT license; 3D models from the Space Kit by Kenney (CC0). The Lampe Games logo is left out, as its license asks. Added to Lab Arcade with touch controls and a back button.

versions.notes: Open RTS by Lampe Games (commit a628ad3, 2025-01-07), security-reviewed, with touch selection, orders and camera.

external.name: Duel Defense
external.tagline: Tower defense: build and upgrade turrets to stop waves of tanks and mechs.
external.about: Enemy tanks and mechs roll along the road towards your base in waves. Spend money on gun, missile and laser turrets beside the road, upgrade them, and earn more for every enemy destroyed. Three maps, rising difficulty, stars for how well you defend, and achievements.
external.controls: Tap a turret at the bottom, then tap a free spot beside the road to place it (drag to move it first). Tap a turret to upgrade or sell it. Play starts the next wave, >> speeds the game up. The menu button pauses. PC: the mouse, Space, F and Esc; also works with a controller.
external.credit: Duel Defense by d10sfan, github.com/duel-defense/duel-defense (d10sfan.itch.io/duel-defense). Code: MIT license. Art and music by Kenney (CC0), craftpix.net, engvee, Matthew Pablo, Zander Noriega, nosoapradio and Alexander Nakarada (CC BY 4.0) and others: see Assets/AssetLicenses. Added to Lab Arcade without the online mod system, with a back button.

versions.notes: Duel Defense by d10sfan (commit b4e5922, 2026-03-16), security-reviewed; the online mod system and start-up command files removed.
Phone layout: the turret shop is a column on the right with big buttons and prices, so nothing covers the map; the map keeps its shape on wide phones (it was stretched); text and buttons bigger.

external.name: Tanks of Freedom II
external.tagline: Turn-based tank battles on voxel maps: capture buildings, build an army, outsmart the AI.
external.about: A turn-based strategy game with voxel art. Move tanks, infantry and helicopters across the map, capture factories and towers for income, build new units and destroy the enemy headquarters. Play the campaigns (with a tutorial), skirmish maps against the computer, or make your own maps in the editor. Online and network play are switched off in Lab Arcade.
external.controls: Tap a unit to select it, then tap where it should move or what it should attack. Tap a building you own to build units. Drag to move the map, pinch to zoom. X cancels a selection. END TURN is on screen. PC: the mouse, right click cancels, wheel zooms.
external.credit: Tanks of Freedom II by P1X (Kamil 'czlowiekimadlo' Marciniak, Krzysztof 'w84death' Jankowski and contributors), github.com/P1X-in/tanks-of-freedom-ii. Code and art: MIT license; music and sounds by QmYaan (CC BY-SA 4.0) and reduz (CC BY 4.0); see LICENSE.md and CREDITS.md. Added to Lab Arcade without online and network play, with touch zoom and a back button.

versions.notes: Tanks of Freedom II by P1X (commit dbe629e, 2025-10-02), security-reviewed; online and network play switched off, trimmed, with pinch zoom.
